'''''The Math Book''''' (Sterling Publishing, 2009. {{ISBN|978-1-4027-5796-9}}) is a book by American author [[Clifford A. Pickover]].

==Summary==

The book contains 250 one-page articles in historical order on milestones in the history of math. Each article is followed by a related full-page color image.  It also contains a bibliography for further reading.

==Reception==
The book has consistently received good reviews<ref>[http://www.johndcook.com/blog/2009/08/30/interview-with-author-cliff-pickover/ johndcook.com]</ref><ref>[http://www.johndcook.com/blog/2009/08/25/math-book-clifford-pickover/ johndcook.com]</ref> although one review mentions a lack of coverage of Chinese accomplishments<ref>[https://old.maa.org/press/periodicals/convergence/review-of-ithe-math-booki maa.org]</ref> and another says "Alas, not all of the great mathematical milestones are included in this book ... Conversely, not all the chosen entries can be considered milestones in mathematics".<ref>[https://old.maa.org/node/110001/ maa.org]</ref>

The book has been praised by [[Martin Gardner]].<ref>[http://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/pickover/math-book.html wisc.edu]</ref>

The book is the winner of the [[British_Society_for_the_History_of_Mathematics#Neumann_Prize|Neumann Prize]].<ref>[https://toronto.overdrive.com/media/847809 The Math Book], Toronto Public Library</ref>

The book has been praised by [[Boing Boing]].<ref>[http://boingboing.net/2009/09/07/the-math-book-from-p.html boingboing.net]</ref>
